title: Throttle
summary: A token-bucket rate limiter with one bucket per API caller.

tasks.title: Huge bursts after a quiet spell
brief: A caller who had been quiet overnight sent several hundred requests in one second and the gateway let them all through, even though buckets hold 20 tokens.
Find out why the limit did not hold and fix it.
done: A bucket never holds more than its capacity, however long it sits idle.
Partial refills still work as before.

questions: After a long idle spell, should the caller get exactly one full burst? (Yes, up to capacity.)
Is the fake clock how production time is modelled in tests? (Yes; the real clock has the same now().)
orient: README states the invariant: “never holds more than capacity”.
Registry only creates and looks up buckets, so the arithmetic must be in bucket.py.
Baseline: all tests pass; none of them leave a bucket idle for long.
walkthrough.failingTest:
def test_idle_time_does_not_overfill():
    clock = FakeClock()
    bucket = TokenBucket(3, 1, clock)
    clock.advance(60)
    assert [bucket.allow() for _ in range(4)] == [True, True, True, False]  # fails: all True
trace: Printed bucket.tokens() after advance(60): 63.0. So the bucket over-fills.
_refill adds elapsed × rate with no upper bound. The invariant is never enforced.
wrapUp: Cause: _refill added elapsed time × rate without capping at capacity.
Fix: wrap the sum in min(capacity, …). One line, plus a regression test.
Checked by hand: half-second refills still give fractional tokens; capacity 1 still works.
With more time: a property-based test that tokens() stays within [0, capacity] for random clocks.

tasks.title: Tell callers when to retry
brief: Rejected callers should get a Retry-After hint. Add TokenBucket.retry_after(cost=1): how many seconds until allow(cost) would succeed, or 0 if it would succeed now.
It must not spend tokens. Asking about a cost bigger than the bucket can ever hold is a programming mistake: raise ValueError.
done: retry_after returns 0 when allowed now, otherwise the exact wait in seconds.
Waiting that long and calling allow(cost) succeeds.
No tokens are spent; impossible costs raise ValueError.

questions: Seconds as a float or rounded up? (A float; the HTTP layer rounds.)
What if cost exceeds capacity? (Raise ValueError; it can never succeed.)
orient: tokens() already refills before reading, so the new method can reuse it rather than touch _refill.
The existing methods validate arguments with ValueError; matched that.
walkthrough.failingTest:
def test_retry_after_says_when_to_come_back():
    bucket = TokenBucket(2, 4, FakeClock())
    bucket.allow(2)
    assert bucket.retry_after() == 0.25
trace: missing = cost − tokens; tokens arrive at rate per second, so the wait is missing / rate, clamped at 0.
wrapUp: Added retry_after built on tokens(), so the refill logic stays in one place.
Verified that waiting the returned time and then calling allow succeeds, which is the property callers rely on.
Noticed but not changed: Registry has no retry_after pass-through yet; the gateway would want one.
